verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन |
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
jyāyasī cet karmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana |
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava || 1 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: If You consider spiritual intellect and knowledge to be superior to action, O Janardana, why then do You urge me to engage in this terrible and violent battle, O Keshava?
verses.meaning: Arjuna is bewildered by what seems to him a contradiction in Sri Krishna's discourse in Chapter 2. Having heard the praise of analytical wisdom (Buddhi Yoga) and equanimity of mind over fruitive action, Arjuna wonders why he must participate in a bloody warfare instead of retiring to peaceful contemplation and ascetic renunciation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे |
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me |
tadekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām || 2 ||
verses.translation: With these seemingly perplexing words, You appear to confuse my intellect. Tell me decisively that one definite path by which I may attain the highest good (Shreyas).
verses.meaning: Arjuna openly expresses his confusion. Seeking absolute clarity rather than dual interpretations of action versus renunciation, he begs Sri Krishna to prescribe the single most spiritually beneficial pathway (Shreyas) for his ultimate spiritual evolution.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ |
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha |
jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām || 3 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: O sinless Arjuna, I have previously declared that in this world there is a two-fold path of spiritual discipline: the Yoga of Knowledge (Jnana Yoga) for contemplative thinkers, and the Yoga of Selfless Action (Karma Yoga) for active practitioners.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna clarifies that Jnana Yoga (contemplation on the Self) and Karma Yoga (selfless dedicated work) are not conflicting paths, but two stages or temperamental approaches designed by the Divine. Both lead to the same spiritual summit of liberation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते |
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo'śnute |
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati || 4 ||
verses.translation: A person does not attain freedom from action (Naishkarmya) merely by abstaining from work, nor does one reach spiritual perfection simply by formal external renunciation.
verses.meaning: Mere physical inertia or running away from worldly duties is not true renunciation. Spiritual freedom (Naishkarmya) is an internal state of desirelessness attained through selfless performance of duty, not through passive avoidance of action.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् |
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt |
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ || 5 ||
verses.translation: Indeed, no one can remain even for a single moment without performing action; for everyone is helplessly driven to act by the qualities born of material nature (Gunas).
verses.meaning: Action is an inescapable law of embodied existence. Breathing, thinking, eating, and metabolic functions are all actions compelled by the three Gunas (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas). Since action is inevitable, wisdom lies in purifying the intention behind action.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् |
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate || 6 ||
verses.translation: One who restrains the organs of action while continuing to dwell upon sense objects in the mind is a deluded soul and is called a hypocrite (Mithyachara).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna sternly warns against pseudo-spirituality. Physically sitting in meditation while mentally craving sensory pleasures is sheer hypocrisy. True mastery begins with mental purity and honest engagement rather than suppressed desires.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन |
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna |
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate || 7 ||
verses.translation: But he who controls the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, and engages the active organs in Karma Yoga without attachment—he is indeed far superior.
verses.meaning: The ideal practitioner lives in the world, actively fulfilling duties through the organs of action while maintaining inner detachment and mental mastery. Such an engaged Karma Yogi is deemed spiritually far superior to the false ascetic.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः |
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ |
śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ || 8 ||
verses.translation: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is indeed superior to inaction. Even the bare maintenance of your physical body would not be possible without action.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna directly commands Arjuna to perform his ordained duty (Niyata Karma). Inaction leads to stagnation, decay, and spiritual decline. Even physical survival requires continuous effort, making disciplined work an essential duty.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः |
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara || 9 ||
verses.translation: Work done as a sacrifice (Yajna) for the Supreme does not bind one to this world. All other work causes bondage. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your duties for the sake of sacrifice, free from all attachment.
verses.meaning: This pivotal verse unlocks the secret of Karma Yoga. Work performed as Yajna (selfless offering to the Divine) ceases to produce karmic bondage. Only ego-driven, self-centered actions bind the soul. Dedicated work becomes worship.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः |
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk || 10 ||
verses.translation: In the beginning, having created humanity along with sacrifice (Yajna), the Creator (Prajapati) declared: 'By this sacrifice shall you prosper; let this be the granter of all your desires (Kamadhuk).'
verses.meaning: Sacrifice and mutual interdependence are woven into the very fabric of cosmic creation. Selfless contribution to the welfare of the collective whole acts like the celestial wish-fulfilling cow (Kamadhuk), ensuring harmony and prosperity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः |
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha || 11 ||
verses.translation: Nourish the celestial beings (Devas) through sacrifice, and let those Devas nourish you in return. By mutually nourishing one another, you shall attain the highest good.
verses.meaning: The universe operates on a reciprocal ecological and spiritual cycle. When humanity respects and nourishes the natural cosmic forces through gratitude and duty, nature reciprocates with abundance, leading to universal well-being.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः |
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ |
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ || 12 ||
verses.translation: Satisfied by sacrifice, the celestial beings will bestow upon you the desired necessities of life. But he who enjoys their gifts without offering anything in return is truly a thief.
verses.meaning: Living purely for selfish consumption while taking from society and nature without giving back is characterized as spiritual theft (Stena). Gratitude, charity, and duty transform enjoyment into a blessed offering.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः |
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ |
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt || 13 ||
verses.translation: The righteous who partake of the remnants of sacrifice (Yajna-shishta) are freed from all sins. But the ungodly, who cook food merely for their own selfish pleasure, truly eat sin.
verses.meaning: Food prepared and offered first to the Divine or shared with the needy (Prasada) purifies the consciousness. Conversely, hoarding and consuming food solely for personal gratification creates karmic entanglement.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः |
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ |
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ || 14 ||
verses.translation: All living beings subsist on food grains; food grains are produced from rains; rains arise from the performance of sacrifice; and sacrifice is born of prescribed duty.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reveals the cosmic wheel of life (Yajna-Chakra). Food sustains living beings; rain sustains agriculture; harmonious ecological action (Yajna) sustains seasonal cycles; and Yajna is born of righteous human labor.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् |
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam || 15 ||
verses.translation: Know that prescribed action originates from the Vedas, and the Vedas arise from the Imperishable Supreme. Therefore, the all-pervading Divine is eternally established in acts of sacrifice.
verses.meaning: Every righteous, selfless duty is rooted in sacred cosmic order. Because the all-pervading Brahman resides in selfless sacrifice, performing our daily duties with reverence connects us directly to the Divine Source.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः |
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati || 16 ||
verses.translation: One who does not help maintain the cosmic wheel thus set in motion in this world leads a sinful life, indulging only in the senses. O Partha, such a person lives in vain.
verses.meaning: Failing to participate in the universal cycle of giving and receiving leads to a wasted life (Mogham). One who lives only for sensual gratification without contributing to the cosmic harmony violates the natural law of existence.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः |
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ |
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate || 17 ||
verses.translation: However, for the soul who rejoices only in the Self, who is completely satisfied with the Self, and who is fully content in the Self alone—for such a person, there remains no obligatory duty.
verses.meaning: The enlightened sage (Jivanmukta), having realized oneness with the Supreme Soul (Atman), has no personal desires or selfish debts left to fulfill. Such an exalted being operates beyond the realm of compulsory karmic obligation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन |
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ || 18 ||
verses.translation: Such a self-realized soul has nothing to gain by the performance of actions, nor anything to lose by non-performance; nor does such a person depend on any created being for any purpose.
verses.meaning: The liberated sage is utterly independent and free from dependency on external outcomes. Whether engaging in actions or remaining silent, their mind remains established in pure transcendental peace.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर |
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ || 19 ||
verses.translation: Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform your obligatory duty with diligence. By performing work without attachment, a person attains the Supreme.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna delivers the foundational precept of Karma Yoga: do not abandon duty, but abandon attachment to the fruits. Selfless, unattached dedication to duty elevates the human mind to supreme enlightenment.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः |
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ |
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi saṃpaśyankartumarhasi || 20 ||
verses.translation: Indeed, King Janaka and other great sages attained supreme perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of guiding the world and maintaining universal welfare (Lokasangraha), you ought to act.
verses.meaning: Krishna cites historical proof: King Janaka governed an entire kingdom with total detachment and attained liberation. Furthermore, leaders must act to set a righteous precedent for the preservation and moral upliftment of society (Lokasangraha).

verses.text_sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः |
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ |
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate || 21 ||
verses.translation: Whatever actions a great person performs, common people follow. Whatever standards of conduct exemplary leaders set, the world conforms to.
verses.meaning: This renowned shloka highlights the profound responsibility of leadership. People emulate the conduct of those they respect. If leaders practice righteousness and dedication, society flourishes; if they shirk duty, chaos ensues.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन |
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana |
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi || 22 ||
verses.translation: O Partha, there is no duty prescribed for Me in all the three worlds, nor is there anything unobtained that I need to attain; yet I remain continuously engaged in action.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna presents Himself as the ultimate role model. As the Supreme Lord of the cosmos, He lacks nothing and desires nothing, yet He tirelessly acts and guides humanity to maintain cosmic harmony and moral order.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः |
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ || 23 ||
verses.translation: For if I did not tirelessly engage in the performance of duty, O Partha, all humanity would immediately follow My path of inaction in every way.
verses.meaning: If the Divine or enlightened role models were to become inactive, people would misuse their example as an excuse for laziness and neglect of dharma, causing widespread moral and spiritual ruin.

verses.text_sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् |
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham |
saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ || 24 ||
verses.translation: If I did not perform My duties, all these worlds would perish in ruin; I would become the author of social chaos and moral confusion, and destroy all these beings.
verses.meaning: Krishna underscores cosmic stewardship. Inaction at the cosmic or leadership level causes disintegration of law, social degradation, and the destruction of civilization.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत |
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṃgraham || 25 ||
verses.translation: As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to results, O descendant of Bharata, so should the wise act with equal zeal, but without attachment, desiring only the welfare and unity of the world.
verses.meaning: The wise do not work with less energy than the ambitious; they work with equal or greater vigor, but their motivation is transformed from selfish greed to selfless service for the good of all creation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् |
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām |
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran || 26 ||
verses.translation: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to fruitive action. Instead, by performing all actions with devotion and discipline, the enlightened should inspire others to fulfill their duties.
verses.meaning: Enlightened teachers should not discourage beginners with abstract philosophies of renunciation that they cannot yet assimilate. Instead, the wise should inspire through personal exemplary action, gradually guiding them toward Karma Yoga.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः |
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartāhamiti manyate || 27 ||
verses.translation: All actions are universally performed by the modes of material nature (Gunas). But the soul deluded by false ego (Ahamkara) mistakenly thinks: 'I am the doer.'
verses.meaning: A monumental philosophical insight: physical, mental, and sensory actions are orchestrated by nature's modes (Prakriti). The pure soul (Atman) is merely the witness. False identification with the ego breeds pride, anxiety, and bondage.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः |
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ |
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate || 28 ||
verses.translation: One who knows the absolute truth regarding the division of the modes of nature and action, O mighty-armed Arjuna, understands that the senses are merely operating among their corresponding sense objects, and remains unattached.
verses.meaning: The seer of truth (Tattva-vit) remains detached, knowing that the senses (modes of Prakriti) are naturally interacting with sense objects. Rooted in the witness consciousness of the immortal Self, the sage remains free from the illusion of doership.

verses.text_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु |
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu |
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet || 29 ||
verses.translation: Those deluded by the modes of nature become deeply attached to the actions and results of those modes. The wise, who possess complete knowledge, should not disturb these people of incomplete understanding.
verses.meaning: Compassion is key in spiritual guidance. Those with partial understanding who are striving through regular duties should not be thrown into confusion by premature demands for renunciation, but helped through gradual purification.

verses.text_sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा |
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā |
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ || 30 ||
verses.translation: Surrendering all your actions unto Me with your mind fixed on the Supreme, free from desire and possessiveness, and liberated from mental fever, engage in battle!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna's supreme practical mandate: Dedicate every action to God (Mayi sannyasya), surrender ownership ('nothing is mine'), let go of anxiety over results (Nirashi), and fulfill your duty with a tranquil, fever-free mind (Vigata-jvara).

verses.text_sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः |
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante te'pi karmabhiḥ || 31 ||
verses.translation: Those who constantly practice this teaching of Mine with deep faith and free from envy—even they become completely liberated from the bondage of all actions.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna offers a divine guarantee: Anyone who lives by this eternal principle of selfless, dedicated action with sincere faith (Shraddha) and a pure heart will attain ultimate spiritual liberation from all karmic reactions.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् |
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ || 32 ||
verses.translation: But those who, out of cynicism and envy, disregard My teaching and do not practice it—know them to be deluded in all knowledge, devoid of discrimination, and ruined.
verses.meaning: Egoistic rejection of divine cosmic law harms only oneself. Those who mock selfless duty remain trapped in endless cycles of selfish desire, anxiety, disappointment, and spiritual ruin.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि |
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi |
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati || 33 ||
verses.translation: Even a person of wisdom acts in accordance with their own innate nature. All living beings follow their natural tendencies; what can mere forceful suppression accomplish?
verses.meaning: Forceful external repression of one's deep psychological nature (Prakriti) is futile and harmful. Spiritual growth requires channelizing one's natural talents through selfless service rather than artificial suppression.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ |
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau |
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau || 34 ||
verses.translation: Attachment (Raga) and aversion (Dvesha) reside naturally in the senses toward their respective objects. One should never come under their sway, for they are obstacles on the spiritual path.
verses.meaning: The twin forces of like and dislike (Raga-Dvesha) distort human judgment and hijack the mind. A spiritual seeker must act out of dharma and duty rather than impulsive cravings or revulsions.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् |
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ || 35 ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own natural duty (Svadharma), though imperfectly executed, than another's duty well-performed. Even death in the performance of one's own duty brings blessing; the duty of another is fraught with danger.
verses.meaning: A cornerstone teaching on personal authenticity and calling. It is spiritually healthier to faithfully pursue one's own natural path and duty (Svadharma)—even with imperfections—than to imitate another's path out of social expectation or fear.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः |
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ || 36 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: By what impelling force, O descendant of Vrishni (Krishna), is a person driven to commit sinful deeds, even against their own will, as if compelled by force?
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks one of the most profound human questions: Why do people knowingly succumb to destructive, immoral actions even when their intellect recognizes the wrongness of the act?

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः |
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ |
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam || 37 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: It is selfish desire (Kama) and anger (Krodha), born of the mode of passion (Rajo-guna). It is all-devouring and deeply sinful; know this to be the greatest enemy in this world.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna identifies the root cause of moral downfall: Kama (insatiable selfish desire). When desire is obstructed, it transforms into raging anger (Krodha). Born of Rajas, this all-consuming fire is the primary internal enemy of the soul.

verses.text_sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च |
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathādarśo malena ca |
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam || 38 ||
verses.translation: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror is obscured by dust, and as an embryo is enveloped within the womb, so is spiritual wisdom covered by selfish desire.
verses.meaning: Krishna provides three vivid analogies for the degree of spiritual obscuration: smoke over fire (easily cleared in Sattvic minds), dust on a mirror (requiring diligent polishing in Rajasic minds), and the womb encasing an embryo (deeply concealed in Tamasic minds).

verses.text_sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा |
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā |
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca || 39 ||
verses.translation: Spiritual wisdom is covered by this eternal enemy of the wise, O son of Kunti, which takes the form of unquenchable desire, burning like an insatiable fire.
verses.meaning: Desire is never extinguished by feeding it sensory fuel; indulging it only makes the fire burn hotter. The wise recognize desire as a perpetual foe that must be mastered through higher spiritual knowledge.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते |
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate |
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam || 40 ||
verses.translation: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are declared to be the seat of this enemy. Through these, desire covers knowledge and deludes the embodied soul.
verses.meaning: To conquer an enemy, one must locate their stronghold. Desire infiltrates through the senses, captures the mind's emotional center, and clouds the discriminating intellect (Buddhi), paralyzing the soul's wisdom.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ |
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha |
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam || 41 ||
verses.translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, by first mastering the senses, slay this sinful destroyer of sacred knowledge and self-realization.
verses.meaning: Krishna lays down the initial line of defense: control the senses first. When the sensory gates are guarded against unhealthy cravings, the mind and intellect remain pure and receptive to spiritual realization.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः |
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ || 42 ||
verses.translation: The senses are said to be superior to the gross physical body; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the immortal Soul (Atman).
verses.meaning: A masterclass in spiritual hierarchy: Body < Senses < Mind < Intellect < Atman. By anchoring consciousness in the supreme, indestructible Soul, one gains mastery over the intellect, the mind, and the senses.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना |
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् || ४३ ||
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā |
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam || 43 ||
verses.translation: Thus knowing the Soul to be higher than the intellect, steadying the mind through the spiritual Self, O mighty-armed Arjuna, conquer this formidable enemy that takes the form of desire!
verses.meaning: The climactic conclusion of Chapter 3: Conquer desire not by brute force, but by awakening to your true identity as the immortal Atman. Rooted in divine consciousness, you can vanquish the illusion of desire and fulfill your sacred destiny.
